name: Dry Tortugas National Park
blurb: Remote reef and sand keys where seabirds nest and turtles graze seagrass.

tip.title: Remove the tiger sharks
tip.text: Tiger sharks are the main predator of green turtles. Set Tiger shark to -100% and watch turtles, then the seagrass and algae they graze.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Dry Tortugas National Park, Sooty tern, Green sea turtle). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A seagrass of shallow sandy flats. Green turtles graze it, and the meadows shelter small fish and invertebrates.

nodes.name: Halimeda algae
nodes.desc: A calcified green alga common on tropical reefs and sand. Grazers such as parrotfish, urchins and turtles feed on algae like it.
Drifting algae in the clear open water around the islands. They feed zooplankton and, through them, the fish that seabirds hunt.
Tiny drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and are eaten by small fish.
A large snail that grazes algae and plant detritus on sand and seagrass beds.
A reef fish that scrapes algae from rock and coral rubble, helping keep algae from smothering the reef.
A plunge-diving bird that eats schooling fish around the islands and roosts on the keys.
A fast reef predator that eats fish such as flyingfish and parrotfish.
A top predator of warm seas that eats sea turtles, fish and seabirds.

nodes.name: Bottlenose dolphin
nodes.desc: Recorded in the park waters. Hunts fish such as schooling and reef fish.
Clear, shallow water lets light reach seagrass, algae and coral on the bottom.

nodes.name: Bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead seagrass, algae and carcasses and return nutrients to the water and sand.

story: Dry Tortugas National Park lies about 68 miles west of Key West in the Gulf of Mexico. Its nominally seven small islands are the westernmost and most isolated of the Florida Keys. The park is known for abundant sea life, tropical bird breeding grounds and coral reefs, and can be reached only by seaplane or boat.
matters: Its coral reefs are the least disturbed of the Florida Keys. Fort Jefferson, the largest brick masonry structure in the Western Hemisphere, stands beside an undisturbed tropical ecosystem.
